title: Alternatives to Ludo for smooth 2D sprite animation, with more generous usage? (student solo dev)
author: yaxir
selftext:
Hi all, I'm a student and a solo dev, working on a 2D action game in Unity. The characters are dense pixel art, about **124 px tall** in game. Hiring an animator isn't within my budget, so I'm relying on AI tools to animate my own key drawings.

I've been using **Ludo.ai (Hydra)**: one key drawing plus a motion prompt. I really like the results: the whole body moves, cloth and hair follow through, and the loops are smooth (this is just one example ofc, but i guess the idea is pretty clear ^^)

My problem is volume. Each main character needs **15–25 moves**, and at about **9 credits per 3-second clip** my monthly credits go quickly. I also tried driving it with a motion reference video, but that came out stiff.

I'd be really grateful for pointers to services or local workflows that are more generous with usage and still give smooth, whole-body motion:

1. Which tools keep a character consistent from **one image** while animating the **whole body**, not just the arms?
2. Does anything offer **per-second pricing, credits that roll over, or an API** for batch jobs?
3. Has anyone had good results with **local open models** (Wan, etc.) for sprite cycles?

Thanks so much for reading!

comments.author: Ferniclestix
comments.body:
Animator here, sorry to hear that.   
it really depends on the pricing of what workflow you are with.  if you can find one that goes by frames then reducing frames is a good idea. human eyes  really don't need that many to get the idea of motion,  we routinely animate on 4's 8's and 12's   rather than going up to the full 25 or 30 you might see on tv.

Local models are a tough sell, you need a good setup, you have to learn how to set it up and you need the hardware. (I did a few tutorials for this kind of thing ages ago on a tool called ComfyUI, you might try looking that up if you want to find stuff for animation in local models. im a bit out of date on that unfortunately)

I will however say this.  if you are not stretched for time, it is possible to make 'tween' frames yourself between poses, the trick is finding a program with a good onion skinning function, putting a frame in the middle and then reproducing your middle image by looking at the images on either side.  its actually a little easier on pixel art because you dont have to freehand anything, its really just a big grid.

seems silly suggesting you just do it by hand I know. but hear me out, the people who get hired on as tween artists are usually not like some pro level artist, its usually just someone who is good at making up the image between one and another. you usually get a primary artist to do the key frames. 

If you do end up with no other recourse. check out 'The animators survival kit" by [Richard E. Williams](https://www.thereallygoodbookshop.com.au/products/author/Richard%20E.%20Williams) \- its basically our bible.

good luck dude.  
Im actually working on a program to do exactly what you need. unfortunately theres no way shes gonna be ready by the time you need.  i have to train some models for it, gonna be really annoying.
